KEY MESSAGE 1...Mainly dry conditions expected today. Increased 
risk for rip currents today, mainly for Cape Cod and Nantucket. 


Mainly dry conditions expected today with weak high pressure 
overhead. Aloft, heights continue to fall today as a mid-level 
trough works into the region while a low pressure system passes well 
offshore. The only "impact" this system will have the region is 
bringing a stream of moisture brushing across mainly the southeast 
portions of MA. This has been prevalent in the low level moisture 
fields with easterly flow to reinforce it. Model soundings indicate 
a shallow layer of moisture at the surface with dry air above. 
Indicator for low clouds and perhaps some patchy drizzle in the 
highest coverage spots. The area that has the greater risk for 
seeing this is Nantucket and perhaps the outer most portion of the 
Cape. Aside from the clouds in some areas, it will be a mainly dry 
day with a northeasterly breeze for the eastern coastal areas. 
Temperatures lean slightly below normal in the upper 70s to low 80s 
for the interior and mid to upper 70s in the eastern and coastal 
areas. Areas such as Nantucket may struggle to get out of the low 
70s today if the clouds stay persistent. 

Prolonged easterly component flow will lead to an increased risk for 
rip currents today. The greatest risk will be for the east-facing 
beaches on Cape Cod and Nantucket; however, there is also an 
elevated risk for the south coast and remaining east-facing beaches. 
Nantucket was added to the current Rip Current Statement. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...Periodic chances of scattered showers and 
thunderstorms early to mid week next week, potentially 
lingering into Thursday. Increasing potential for heavy rain 
late Tuesday through Wednesday with at least localized flash 
flooding possible.

A mid-level trough positions across the region through much of the 
week. A series of shortwaves embedded in the flow are expected to 
progress across the region through the week supporting periodic 
chances for showers and thunderstorms. 

The first embedded shortwave likely moves through late Monday into 
Tuesday. WAA and moist advection occur ahead of the shortwave during 
the day Monday resulting in a warmer day in the low to mid 80s and 
upper 70s for coastal areas. There is still potential for scattered 
showers and thunderstorms late afternoon/evening though guidance is 
still lacking agreement on the coverage and convective potential. 
This keeps us at probabilities less than 40% still with west/central 
southern New England being more favored. 

Model guidance has remained generally consistent with a deepening 
trough into Tue/Wed with a strong signal for above normal moisture 
(120-170% of normal) advecting into the region by Tuesday. Most 
deterministic and ensemble solutions have now come on board with the 
development of a low pressure system. In many solutions now, the low 
pressure is quite anomalous in magnitude for late-July. Combined 
with the enhanced forcing from the low, this is a set-up for heavy 
rain potential. However, some model guidance has been more 
aggressive than others. The ECMWF and its ensemble members have 
shown the strongest signal for heavy rain/flash flooding potential 
with a stronger low pressure system tracking in the vicinity of Long 
Island, toward eastern MA/Cape Cod in many of its solutions. It also 
leans on a slower progression of the trough as well. Soundings 
exhibit the textbook environment for efficient rain processes with 
deep warm cloud depths aligned with instability. ECMWF ens probs 
show 40-75% probability for 1+ of rainfall later Tue into Wed and 10-
40% for 2"+ across a good portion of southern New England. The 
deterministic guidance over the last 24 hours of runs has showed a 
large footprint of 2"+ amounts across the region in that same 
timeframe. With weak steering flow this support slow storm motions 
of embedded heavy rain and thunderstorms. This combined with 
potential for training for training will increase the risk for flash 
flooding with more "scattered" occurrences as opposed to an 
isolated case or two. While the recent deterministic runs of the
Canadian and GFS have gone more on board with the heavy rain 
potential, their ensemble guidance still have shown solutions 
leaning toward a weaker low and differing track resulting 
leading to lesser rainfall amounts. There is still a signal for 
localized heavy rain/flash flooding within these solutions; 
however, they are more isolated or localized. There is still 
uncertainty; however, we are at least seeing increasing 
confidence for widespread rain with at least localized heavy 
downpours/flash flooding possible in spots, particularly later 
Tue through Wed. Depending on the track of the low, showers may 
linger through Thurs. 

Temperatures lean seasonably cool to slightly below normal at times 
through the week ranging in the mid 70s to low 80s.
